summary: tooldef: RoleToolDefinitionInput is missing profile?; runtime reads it via a cast (define-tool.ts:435) — causes promote.ts:209 TS2769
body:
Surfaced during the systems-abstraction code audit (not a systems-abstraction defect — flagging for the defineTool/tooldef owners per D-001).

Type↔runtime mismatch in @papercusp/tooldef:
- registerRoleGatedAsProjected reads `profile` off a role tool via a CAST: `profile: (def as { profile?: 'engineer' | 'all' }).profile` (packages/tooldef/src/define-tool.ts:435) and projects it — so profile-gating IS honored on role-gated tools at runtime.
- But the RoleToolDefinitionInput type does NOT declare `profile?` (only the plain ToolDefinitionInput overload has it, types.ts:329/381). So any role tool that sets profile fails defineTool overload resolution with TS2769 "No overload matches this call".
- Sole symptom in the tree: apps/operator/lib/agent-tools/coordination/tools/promote.ts:209 (a role tool: roles+capability+requirePrincipal) that also sets `profile: 'engineer'` (line 211).

Fix (tooldef-owned): add `profile?: 'engineer' | 'all'` to RoleToolDefinitionInput (+ RoleToolDefinition), then drop the cast at define-tool.ts:435. Behavior-safe; makes the type match what the runtime already does. NOT fixable operator-side without un-gating promote (removing profile = behavior change), so leaving promote.ts as-is.
